title: Cohortwise Canary Orchestrator and Shadow-Fork Sentinel
creator: Sophia Patel
description:
Problem: Current model rollouts use coarse traffic splits and global statistical checks which miss localized regressions in key cohorts (e.g., mobile users, regional dialects, premium customers). We need an orchestration layer that: 1) creates adaptive cohorts for canaries, 2) runs non-invasive shadow forks to collect unlabeled signals, 3) applies sequential statistical checks (both frequentist and Bayesian options) per-cohort, and 4) can auto-sheriff (automatic gated rollback) when safety thresholds trigger.

Goal: Deliver a production-ready A/B/canary framework that runs at per-request granularity, supports shadow-mirroring, provides clear per-cohort health signals in the Console, and supports configurable automatic rollback policies with audit logs and multi-tenant guardrails.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Orchestrator can be configured to create cohorts by attributes (region, device, tenant tier, prompt fingerprint).
2) Shadow fork mode supports 100% mirroring of live requests to a candidate variant without affecting response path and captures metrics (latency, token cost, quality proxies).
3) Sequential statistical checks implemented: SPRT and a conjugate-Bayesian sequential test; both available as options with configurable alpha/beta.
4) Console shows per-cohort time-series and a single 'sheriff' status: OK / Watch / Auto-RolledBack.
5) Auto-rollback executes a documented playbook: pause routing, revert to baseline variant, notify oncall, and create incident ticket.
6) End-to-end tests (integration + canary e2e) that simulate cohort regressions and validate rollback behavior.
7) RBAC for canary controls and audit logs available for Private deployments.
success_metrics:
- Detect and rollback injected cohort-level regressions >95% of the time within first 30 minutes in synthetic tests.
- Reduce manual rollback interventions by 70% for staged releases.
- Mean time to detect cohort regressions across canaries < 12 minutes in production telemetry (after rollouts enabled).
- No customer-facing error rate increase attributable to shadow mirroring or orchestration.
technical_approach:
1) Scheduler: build a stateful canary scheduler that assigns cohorts using a lightweight fingerprinting library (client request attributes => stable cohort id).
2) Shadow forks: implement stateless mirroring proxy that forwards requests to candidate runtime with isolated tracing and sampling to avoid KV cache pollution. Mirror responses land in a sandboxed telemetry pipeline (no impact to live cache/state).
3) Statistical engine: wrap SPRT + Bayesian sequential test in a microservice (experiment-evaluator) that consumes aggregated per-cohort stats from metrics pipeline and emits signal events (WATCH/FAIL/PASS) to the orchestrator.
4) Auto-sheriff: orchestrator policy engine implements graded actions (increase monitoring, reduce exposure, pause rollout, immediate rollback) and executes via routing control APIs.
5) Observability: extend Console with per-cohort dashboards, event log for policy decisions, and per-request lineage links to traces/PRs.
6) Safety: require multi-signal confirmation (e.g., quality proxy + latency or token cost) for automatic rollback in enterprise tenants; soft-fallback to baseline variant when auto-rollback fired.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (2 weeks): spec + design PRD, experiment-evaluator prototype, simple cohorting library, and shadow-mirroring PoC on non-critical tenant.
Phase 2 (4 weeks): integrate with routing control, implement SPRT, expose Console widgets, and run synthetic canary tests.
Phase 3 (3 weeks): implement auto-sheriff policies (graded actions), RBAC, and audit logs; run closed beta with internal teams.
Phase 4 (ongoing): staged customer launches, gather metrics, iterate on thresholds and UI affordances.
Gate for Phase 3 -> hard requirement: documented rollback playbook and runbook drill completed by SRE and Solutions Eng teams.
risks:
- Shadow mirroring could increase backend load if not rate-limited; mitigated by sampling and sandboxed execution.
- False positives from sensitive metrics (e.g., transient latency spikes) triggering rollback; mitigated by multi-signal confirmation and minimum exposure windows.
- KV cache side effects if mirrored requests hit shared state; mitigated using stateless sandbox routing and cache key namespacing.
- Regulatory/tenanted concerns for Private deployments; requires KMS/audit controls before enabling auto-rollback for regulated customers.
